prose: Why does Nathan Oakley say the globe needs a flat Earth? The author of Measured Flat: All Roads Lead to Flat Earth joins Chance Garton on InnerVerse to explore his argument that the globe model depends on fundamental flat measurements. What does an elevation angle actually measure? Why do you level a compass, and why are north and up different directions? Nathan connects these questions to celestial navigation, sextants, Polaris, and the distinction between observation, calculation, and scientific experimentation.
ext: Nearly an hour of additional discussion exploring calculations of the distance to the sun, gas pressure and containment, gravity, and the burden of proof. Nathan also turns his criticism toward Tartaria, mud-flood narratives, and the incentives shaping online conspiracy content.
